description.summary: A bold trick-taking game — win your exact target number of tricks, or none at all.

content.title: Overview
content.text: Braggart is a trick-taking game for 3-5 players. The deck has three suits — Brains, Speed, and Strength — numbered 1-11, plus a few Pass cards. Each round you are dealt 7 cards and play 7 tricks. The catch: you only score by winning the exact target number of tricks, or by winning none at all.

content.title: The shifting hierarchy
content.text:
At all times the three suits sit in a strength order shown in the middle of the table: Strongest, Middle, and Weakest. ANY card of a stronger suit beats ANY card of a weaker suit — the number only matters to break ties within the same suit.

The twist: after each trick, the winning suit immediately drops to Weakest. So the pecking order is always rotating.

content.title: Playing a trick
content.text:
The trick leader plays any suit; everyone else must follow that suit if they can. The trick is won by the strongest-suit card played (ties broken by the higher number). The winner leads the next trick.

Because a stronger off-suit card beats the led suit, you can steal a trick even when you can't follow!

content.title: Pass cards
content.text: Instead of following suit, you may play a Pass card. A Pass never wins a trick and hides whether you could have followed — perfect for ducking a trick you don't want.

content.title: Scoring
content.text:
At the end of each round you score for tricks won:
2 points for winning ZERO tricks.
1 point for winning EXACTLY the target: 3 tricks with 3 players, 2 with 4 players, 1 with 5 players.
0 points for anything else. Overshoot or undershoot your boast and you get nothing!

content.title: Most points wins
content.text: Braggart is played over multiple rounds. After each round you vote whether to play again; when the table decides to stop, the player with the most total points wins (ties share the win).

content.title: Turn order & timeouts
content.text: Play proceeds clockwise from the trick leader. Your current trick count for the round is shown as your 🃏 score. If you run out of time to play, a random legal card is played for you.
